resync_trigger: Review the upstream procedure diff before upgrading the external analyser from 0.9.20.

resync_triggers.trigger: The installed the external analyser is upgraded past 0.9.20.
resync_triggers.mechanism: Read the new crate's own .cargo_vcs_info.json for the commit it was published from (no guessing at a tag), fetch the five procedure paths at that commit from the GitHub repository, sha256 each, and diff against this manifest's per-procedure sha256 values. Any digest that moved means the absorbed prose at that destination must be re-read against upstream before the upgrade is accepted. anno-derivation.test.ts's live-gated re-hash check performs the comparison half when ANNO_UPSTREAM_CLONE points at a clone of the pinned tree (that test was renamed from the pre-Phase-29 upstream-audit test by plan 29-05; the environment-variable name above is deliberately unchanged across that rename, because an environment variable is a name CI binds by and renaming one silently turns a hard-gated check into a skipped one).

AppState::file_info() already computes packer_name and is_packed and throws them away before the handler's json! block. The day either reaches that block, SURF-03's packer finding collapses to a one-field read and its external unp64 oracle becomes unnecessary (SURF-03 is a Phase 19 requirement id from a retired family and no longer resolves against the current REQUIREMENTS.md; it is kept because it names the finding this trigger watches, and the finding itself survives -- see packer-finding.mjs). Watch by calling anno_get_binary_info after any upgrade and diffing the returned key set against the seven fields recorded in 19-RESEARCH.md section 2.2(a).

resync_triggers.trigger: A future phase needs an upstream call this manifest currently disposes of as omitted.
resync_triggers.mechanism: Every non-curated call has a disposition_rationale entry below carrying the reason it was left out. Two of them (anno_toggle_splitter, anno_set_immediate_format) already name the requirement that WOULD supply their criterion; a third (anno_undo) names the criterion that ARRIVED and was discharged without a surface verb, which makes its omission a decided one rather than a pending one. Adding one to CURATED_ANNO_TOOLS requires updating that entry's disposition in the same commit, so the manifest cannot silently disagree with src/mcp/vice/anno-tools.ts.

anno_get_disassembly_cursor.justification: Upstream's own text forbids the cursor route in exactly the situation this project's absorbed procedure describes, and this project has no editor cursor at all. The caller always supplies an explicit address, and anno_read_region (SURF-01, D18-24/D18-25) answers 'read this routine' by range. The retired analyser's own tool registry recorded the trio as HELD, not unproven (D18-26): the absorption diff produced a caller whose own upstream text says not to use it, so the tool stayed HELD and that was the recorded reason. That module was deleted in Phase 29 and the surviving src/mcp/vice/anno-tools.ts carries no equivalent HELD record, so this sentence is a dated past-tense fact about the Phase 19 pin and not a route to follow. (SURF-01 above is likewise a Phase 19 requirement id from a retired family and no longer resolves against the current REQUIREMENTS.md; it is kept because it records which requirement answered the read-by-range route at the pin.)
anno_get_disassembly_cursor.upstream_citation: an upstream program procedure:74 and :128 -- "**CRITICAL**: Always launch each subagent with an explicit target address ... **NEVER** use the 'current cursor address' or rely on the active cursor location in the editor"

anno_undo.justification: anno_set_data_type is idempotent over a range, so upstream's 'if a conversion was wrong, undo it and redo it correctly' collapses to 'set it correctly'. The retired analyser's own tool registry recorded undo/redo as earning no place under this surface's discipline even once a session persisted; that module was deleted in Phase 29 and the surviving src/mcp/vice/anno-tools.ts carries no equivalent record, so this sentence is a dated past-tense fact about the Phase 19 pin and not a route to follow. The criterion v0.7.0 supplies for this call is STORE-04, and it ARRIVED and was DISCHARGED rather than left open: STORE-04's 'an edit can be reverted' is answered at the store layer by whole-store snapshot/restore -- revertTo(handle, revision) in src/mcp/vice/anno-store.ts -- and deliberately NOT exposed as a surface verb, per decision D2, which also records a per-edit inverse-command undo journal as permanently Out of Scope (zero callers measured, and Node's sqlite exposes no sqlite3changeset_invert). So the omission STANDS, and what changed about this record is that it is now a DECIDED omission with a named criterion rather than an unexamined one.
anno_undo.upstream_citation: an upstream blocks procedure:85 -- "if a conversion was wrong, use `anno_undo` to revert"

anno_toggle_splitter.justification: Future-surface proposal, not a permanent omission, and it blocks Phase 20/21 rather than Phase 19 (those phase numbers are from a superseded roadmap and do not resolve against the current ROADMAP.md; they are kept because they record when the block was expected to bite). Without a splitter, two adjacent same-type tables auto-merge into one block, so DECOMP-01's 'every byte is code, byte, word, address, PETSCII, screencode or table' cannot distinguish them and BUILD-02's 'data tables extracted to their own files' has no boundary to cut on. It also biases COV-01's divergence sub-report: anno_get_blocks 'Respects splitters', so the store side will show a systematic over-merge that must be reported as a named bias rather than instrument error. Propose it additively, in SURF-01's pattern, sequenced so Phase 20 has it (SURF-01 is a Phase 19 requirement id from a retired family and no longer resolves against the current REQUIREMENTS.md). SUPERSEDED at the Phase 28 store: STORE-02 closed this entry's named blocker BY CONSTRUCTION -- ranges are stored as ranges and are never merged on adjacency, so no splitter concept is needed, none is introduced, and the systematic over-merge bias predicted above for COV-01 cannot now occur. The proposal is therefore not pending: it is designed out rather than worked around. DECOMP-01 and BUILD-02 both remain LIVE requirement ids, re-mapped from v0.7.0 to v0.9.0 on 2026-08-26, which is why they are kept below unchanged.
anno_toggle_splitter.upstream_citation: an upstream blocks procedure:158 and Pitfall 5 -- "**Forgetting splitters**: Two adjacent byte tables will auto-merge into one. Use `anno_toggle_splitter` at the boundary."; handler.rs:188 -- anno_get_blocks's description states "Respects splitters."

anno_set_immediate_format.justification: Future-surface proposal, not a permanent omission, and it blocks Phase 21 (that phase number is from a superseded roadmap and does not resolve against the current ROADMAP.md; it is kept because it records when the block was expected to bite). It is the low/high-byte pointer-readability step: "format": "low_byte" / "high_byte" plus "target_address" turns a split immediate load into a symbol reference, which is literally BUILD-03's requirement that every branch, JSR/JMP and data reference goes through a symbol so code can move. The retired analyser's own tool registry recorded 'no criterion in this phase' at the pin; that module was deleted in Phase 29 and the surviving src/mcp/vice/anno-tools.ts carries no equivalent record, so this sentence is a dated past-tense fact and not a route to follow. BUILD-03 is the criterion the absorption diff supplies. Its upstream implementation is mutating (applies a Command, calls perform_analysis() and disassemble(), pushes a Batch), and the discipline such an addition would answer to on this surface is the Phase 28 store's SINGLE-WRITER one rather than any session mutex: no session exists to hold a queue, because the store is opened and closed within one tool call (D-06), and a caller that must not clobber a concurrent edit passes the optional base_revision compare-and-swap argument, whose validator in src/mcp/vice/anno-tools.ts refuses a non-integer by name rather than leaving it to SQLite's column affinity.
anno_set_immediate_format.upstream_citation: an upstream program procedure:84 and :140 -- "apply low/high byte formatting (`anno_set_immediate_format`) to any immediate pointer loads"; upstream implementation at crates/external-analyser-core/src/mcp/handler.rs:1645-1695

anno_unpack_binary.justification: Explicit omission, permanent. The call is destructive by upstream's own description and by its implementation (the handler calls app_state.load_unpacked_binary(...), replacing the binary in place), and this project has a non-destructive route to the same answer: c64-ram-capture runs the program in the emulator and captures RAM past the decrunch, plus SURF-03's packer-identity finding (SURF-03 is a Phase 19 requirement id from a retired family and no longer resolves against the current REQUIREMENTS.md; the finding it names survives as a dated provenance record in packer-finding.mjs). The entropy gate upstream wraps around it SURVIVES the omission, because entropy is a field of anno_get_binary_info's live response and the 7.5 threshold is written into the curated tool description.
anno_unpack_binary.upstream_citation: an upstream program procedure:31 -- "`anno_unpack_binary` is a destructive action (clears existing comments/labels/blocks) and may take up to 10 seconds or more"; upstream implementation at crates/external-analyser-core/src/mcp/handler.rs:844-852
